newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread squeezed up after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread squeezed up after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Britain's Whitbread Plc were squeezed higher in thin trade on Wednesday after in-line results from the brewing-to-hotels group coupled with an upbeat trading statement, dealers said.

"The results were generally in line and the stock has been squeezed a bit higher," said one market-maker, "the figures weren't sparkling but they have probably alerted all the bears in this stock that things are basically allright."
Whitbread shares were up 11-1/2p at 801-1/2 by 0916 GMT in moderate trade of 1.2 million shares.
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose 12 percent to 316.5 million stg, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range between 313 million stg and 321 million.
Chairman Sir Michael Angus said it had been a strong trading performance across the group.
"The recent acquisitions have given Whitbread the best brand range in our chosen markets," he said. "The beer company once again outperformed the market to achieve its highest ever share."
Angus said trading in the new financial year had continued to be robust and in line with expectations.
